title: Intrathecal baclofen — abrupt withdrawal or overdose
effect: Seizures with withdrawal, with overdose, and at therapeutic doses (Gablofen §5.5)
Convulsion on maintenance infusion: 4.7% (spinal origin), 10.0% (cerebral origin) in trials (Gablofen §6.1, Tables 1–2)
pearls: AVOID = avoid abrupt interruption (boxed warning: "Do not discontinue abruptly")
Abrupt stop → high fever, altered mental status, rebound spasticity, rigidity; rarely rhabdomyolysis, multiorgan failure, death (boxed warning)
Early withdrawal: return of spasticity, pruritus, hypotension, paresthesias; onset hours to a few days (§5.5)
Advanced withdrawal can resemble autonomic dysreflexia, sepsis, malignant hyperthermia or NMS (§5.5)
Common causes: catheter malfunction (especially disconnection), low reservoir volume, pump battery end of life (§5.5)
Higher risk: spinal cord injury at T6 or above, communication difficulties, prior withdrawal (boxed warning)
Treat withdrawal: restore intrathecal baclofen at or near the prior dose; if delayed, oral/enteral baclofen or oral/enteral/IV benzodiazepines — oral baclofen alone isn't enough (§5.5)
Overdose: drowsiness, respiratory depression, seizures, rostral hypotonia, coma up to 72 h; no antidote — remove residual drug from the pump, intubate if needed (§10)
Overdose: physostigmine 2 mg IM/IV at ≤1 mg/min may reverse drowsiness and respiratory depression (anecdotal), but can induce seizures and bradycardia (§10)
Overdose: if LP not contraindicated, consider withdrawing 30–40 mL CSF (§10)
